Its native Rust core provides efficient implementations of circuit processing, quantum-state and operator computation, compilation, and optimization, while Python and C interfaces support algorithm development and system integration. Cqlib covers quantum program construction, simulation, analysis, compilation, device adaptation, and result processing under consistent program semantics. Through OpenQASM and the Quantum Control Instruction Set (QCIS), Cqlib supports program representation and hardware-oriented execution. Cqlib further provides backend interfaces for device execution, with Cqlib-Tianyan serving as one implementation for QCIS-compatible quantum hardware. Evaluations using parameterized compilation tasks from Benchpress and related tests show that Cqlib achieves good functional coverage, compilation correctness, and execution efficiency within the evaluated task scope. We develop Cqlib-Algorithm as a modular library of reusable operators and composable components for widely used quantum algorithms, including quantum search, phase estimation, and variational algorithms, with additional support for error mitigation. To complement these building blocks with domain-specific workflows, we further develop Cqlib-VQE, Cqlib-QAOA, and Cqlib-QML for application-level studies in quantum chemistry, combinatorial optimization, and quantum machine learning, respectively. Cqlib also integrates source-grounded Skills and MCP-based tools to support agent-assisted program generation, backend execution, and result-guided workflow refinement. Overall, Cqlib provides a unified and extensible software foundation that connects quantum algorithm development, simulation, compilation, and execution on QCIS-compatible quantum hardware.
authors: Tianyan Quantum Group

papers.title: Multiphoton Electronic Coherences in Molecules
papers.abstract: We investigate multiphoton electronic coherences in a series of gas-phase atomic and molecular systems with increasing complexity. Our measurements are driven by pairs of phase-locked, deep-ultraviolet pulses with independent control of the relative phase and time delay. By combining the ionization yields measured at specific relative phases between the pulses, we can isolate different multiphoton orders and enable measurements of coherences between specific pairs of electronic states. We measure electronic coherences between states separated by zero-photon (i.e. within our laser bandwidth), one-photon and two-photons, resulting in signals with modulation periods ranging from 430 attoseconds to several femtoseconds. Fast electronic dynamics are tracked simultaneously with the accompanying nuclear motion. Additionally, we derive analytic expressions for the measured ionization yield as a function of pump-probe delay and demonstrate their use as a quantitative tool for isolating individual photon-order contributions within the total yield.
authors: Loc Thi-Hoang Ngo, Brian Kaufman, Varun Makhija, Ryan Cloughly, Javin Ohara, Julia Codere, Scott Liguori, Sameer Singh, Martin Cohen, Matt Bain, Brett Pearson, Ruaridh Forbes, Thomas Weinacht

papers.title: Spin-adapted state preparation for quantum chemistry
papers.abstract: Quantum phase estimation for strongly-correlated molecules requires an initial state of high overlap with the true ground state, and preparing one is a significant fault-tolerant cost. Matrix product states (MPS) produced by the density matrix renormalisation group (DMRG) are a leading choice, yet existing circuits treat their tensors as dense or do not use the full symmetries present in molecular electronic Hamiltonians. In quantum chemistry, DMRG also exploits total spin, a non-abelian symmetry, storing one amplitude per spin multiplet instead of one per state. We show that the reduced tensors of such a spin-adapted MPS, labelled by the steps of the unitary group approach, form an abelian-symmetric MPS, which existing block-sparse preparation protocols can load at a cost set by the multiplet count. One state-independent rotation per site, determined by a Clebsch-Gordan coefficient, then returns the state to the occupation basis. We provide resource estimates for our circuits on singlet ground states of active space models of iron-sulphur clusters, finding improvements in Toffoli count up to $135\times$ compared to dense methods and $4.9\times$ compared to block-sparse methods applied to the same states, with up to $3.7\times$ fewer ancilla qubits required.
authors: Matthew L. Sims-Goh, Fredrik Hasselgren, Hamza Jnane

papers.title: Quantum Amplitude Estimation for Ligand and Pose Index Retrieval
papers.abstract: Structure-based virtual screening spans a combinatorial configuration space, motivating a quantum screening framework that targets threshold-qualified configuration indices without reconstructing a complete interaction-score table. Quantum amplitude estimation based on quantum phase estimation (QAE/QPE) supplies finite-resolution phase information to a reversible comparator that writes its decision to FLAG, while optional Grover-style quantum selection (QSEL) amplifies FLAG-selected outcomes and selector measurements identify the ligand, receptor state, rotation, and translation. In an ideal logical benchmark using AutoDock grid interactions as a proof-of-concept model, we evaluated initial FLAG acceptance probability, classification precision, shots required for 95% FLAG detection, and logical Q-operator calls across eight receptor systems and nested libraries of up to 1,024 ligand occupancies. Higher QAE/QPE resolution generally improved classification precision at additional evaluation cost, whereas suitably chosen QSEL iteration counts reduced required shots without improving classification precision, revealing selection and resource trade-offs for extending coherent index retrieval to more physically detailed molecular evaluation models.
authors: Pei-Kun Yang

papers.title: Super-Multiplicativity of the Noncommutative Minimum and Applications to Quantum Privacy and Hypothesis Testing
papers.abstract: The hockey-stick divergence is a fundamental distinguishability measure in quantum information theory. It characterizes quantum differential privacy and determines the optimal error probability of binary quantum hypothesis testing with arbitrary priors. We study how it behaves on tensor-product states. To this end, we consider the noncommutative minimum $m(A,B):=(\mathrm{Tr}[A]+\mathrm{Tr}[B]-\|A-B\|_1)/2$ of positive semidefinite operators, which reduces to $\sum_x\min\{a_x,b_x\}$ when $A$ and $B$ commute, and we prove that it is super-multiplicative, i.e., $m(A\otimes C,B\otimes D)\ge m(A,B)\,m(C,D)$. As a consequence, we establish a sub-additivity property of the hockey-stick divergence on product states, in which the parameters of the individual systems are multiplied, and no additional prefactor appears. We show that this bound is tight, also for noncommuting states, and that it is strict for faithful states whenever at least two of the divergences are positive. Using this, we obtain sub-additivity of the Datta-Leditzky divergences, a parallel composition theorem for quantum differentially private channels under product neighboring inputs with at most linear degradation of the privacy parameters, and a sharp sub-additivity property of the hypothesis-testing relative entropy normalized by the acceptance probability. Finally, we apply the same tools to symmetric binary quantum hypothesis testing. We determine the exact prefactor of the quantum Chernoff bound for every pair of noncommuting states satisfying mild conditions including a nonlattice condition and, under a quantitative version of this condition, the full asymptotic expansion to every fixed order in $1/n$, with explicitly computable coefficients. As a consequence, we determine the sample complexity of symmetric binary quantum hypothesis testing up to one sample, as the error probability tends to zero.
authors: Theshani Nuradha, Sujeet Bhalerao, Christoph Hirche, Mark M. Wilde, Mingze Xu

papers.title: Geometric Polarization-Virial Theorems for Field-Induced Dipolar Interactions and Force Reversal
papers.abstract: Electric fields can turn attraction into repulsion between far-separated atoms, yet the complete angular mechanical structure governing this reversal has remained unknown. Here, we uncover an entropy-like geometric structure: the cubically weighted interaction free energy, r^3 F(r), is nondecreasing under physical dilation. This structure unifies two exact polarization-virial theorems for arbitrary stable quasistatic dipole assemblies and fully retarded dipole pairs under stated conditions. Consequently, the free energy has at most one zero and energetic cancellation precedes mechanical cancellation. A force zero retains strictly positive energy, whereas an energy zero retains an attractive force. The resulting analytical angular fine structure is resolved by a quantum harmonic oscillator pair, yielding the complete arbitrary-angle interaction energy and radial force that recover quantum-perturbative results. The conventional dipolar magic angle splits into strictly ordered energy- and force-zero angles; the latter uniquely bounds the radially repulsive sector and carries a positive energy barrier. Derived scaling laws and finite-sphere calculations provide experimentally testable signatures from microscopic dipoles to macroscopic polarizable bodies.
authors: Shuze Zhu

papers.title: Domain advantage in two-dimensional quantum-device design with multi-modal agentic harness
papers.abstract: High-quality two-dimensional quantum devices are commonly fabricated from mechanically exfoliated crystals, whose irregular shapes and placement require a lithographic layout tailored to each specimen. Drawing these layouts remains largely manual. We introduce qlaybench, a benchmark that tests whether language-model agents can turn microscope images and experimental requirements into device layouts that fit the specimen. Agents with conventional tools often construct devices when material outlines are supplied, but struggle to identify those outlines from images. Modelled on the human workflow, qlaybot, a multimodal agentic harness, connects image interpretation to the tools used to align images, draw device features and inspect the resulting layout. We evaluate each layout with checks drawn from practical design experience, asking whether it fits the specimen and connects its intended components. With greater computational effort, an agent using qlaybot passes 81.5% of the benchmark tasks, compared with 24.1% when it uses conventional tools. This domain advantage highlights the importance of connecting scientific interpretation of a specimen to geometric design and provides a route towards reducing manual effort in two-dimensional quantum-device fabrication.
authors: Shenhao Miao, Yizhou Li, Liqiao Xia, Ruihao Liu, Dingke Wang, Pablo Jarillo-Herrero, Eli Zeldov, Jiaqi Cai

papers.title: The response field approach to path integral control
papers.abstract: This paper investigates non-linear path integral control problems within the response field formalism of nonequilibrium field theory. The aim of this work is exploratory, based on the identification of correspondences between backward adjoint processes and the response field of non-equilibrium statistical physics, whose properties have not been set out in an optimal control setting. The response field is found to play an analogous role to the backward adjoint process under the stochastic maximum principle. In particular, the gradient of the optimal cost-to-go at the initial time, which is proportional to the optimal control, is given by the average of the response field at the initial time. In contrast to the case of non-equilibrium dynamics, the response function is found to be acausal in the control setting. The linear-quadratic case of path integral control is studied, confirming it as the free theory, meaning that solving the control problem is equivalent to completing the square and determining the propagator for a two point boundary value problem. The developments presented here are a necessary prelude to applications based on field theoretic approximation, for both path integral control and their dual inference problems.
authors: George Stamatescu

papers.title: Trajectory arclength reveals thermodynamic criticality
papers.abstract: Thermodynamic criticality arises at continuous phase transitions, where collective interactions produce non-analytic behavior in equilibrium thermodynamic quantities in the thermodynamic limit. We show that this criticality also leaves an analytically predictable signature in the arclength of microscopic Hamiltonian trajectories. For the attractive Hamiltonian mean-field model, we derive the thermodynamic limit of the equilibrium-averaged arclength, formulated as a normalized Lagrangian descriptor, and demonstrate that it develops a kink precisely at the phase transition. We trace this non-analyticity to spontaneous magnetization and derive the leading critical finite-size correction, scaling as $N^{-1/2}$ with an explicit analytical prefactor. Simulations with up to $10^5$ degrees of freedom confirm both predictions without adjustable parameters. Requiring neither tangent-space evolution nor prior specification of an order parameter for its computation, trajectory arclength provides a simple, quantitative link between microscopic Hamiltonian motion and collective thermodynamic criticality.
authors: Jim\'enez-L\'opez, Javier, Garc\'ia-Garrido, V. J

papers.title: Solids activated by multi-body nonreciprocity
papers.abstract: Field-mediated forces between particles can be both nonreciprocal and irreducibly multi-body, giving rise to emergent activity in systems of individually passive particles. While prior work extensively studied how multi-body nonreciprocity can activate few-body systems, fuel intermittency, and drive liquid-like behavior, the effect on the solid state of large particle ensembles is less explored. Here we use two-dimensional, close-packed rafts of identical, athermal, acoustically levitated microspheres to show how multi-body nonreciprocity injects activity in solids. At the level of both individual particles and collective dynamics, crystalline rafts exhibit persistent circulations with no net handedness. The rafts also exhibit a phonon-like dispersion relation corresponding to a large Poisson ratio, indicating an induced softness to shear. Within the bulk, lattice symmetry masks microscopic nonreciprocity, although it can manifest in renormalized, reciprocal elastic coefficients. At dislocations and raft edges, where this symmetry is broken, multi-body nonreciprocal interactions act as local generators of activity. A coarse-grained microscopic model of multi-body nonreciprocity, calibrated on three-particle simulations, recovers the rafts' experimentally observed dispersion relations and localized activity. Using these findings, we illustrate how to harness defect-induced activity for programmable movement by arranging microscopic dislocations to drive macroscopic propulsion and rotation of a whole raft.
authors: Brady Wu, Daniel S. Seara, Qinghao Mao, Vincenzo Vitelli, Heinrich M. Jaeger

papers.title: Reconstructing Pure-State OTOCs from Forward-Time Linear Response
papers.abstract: We show that the connected out-of-time-ordered correlator (OTOC) of any pure state can be reconstructed exactly from commutator linear responses alone. The protocol requires no time reversal, no ancilla, no double copy, and no weak measurement: a unitary string pulse, forward many-body evolution, and a single local readout suffice. An average over a complete basis of pulse generators yields the OTOC exactly. We further show that the measurement can be made sparse by restricting the pulses to a fixed operator weight, which turns the truncation into an analytically controlled spectral filter: the deterministic bias can be computed before the experiment and cleanly separated from the statistical sampling variance. For Gaussian states, the finite-weight response is exactly proportional to the full OTOC after a known combinatorial rescaling. For quantum chaotic systems, the typical residual is suppressed as a power law in the sector size. Exact-diagonalization benchmarks in the Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev model and a nonintegrable Ising chain confirm these predictions.
authors: Yu-Hang Jin, Xudong He, Yu Chen

papers.title: A Steady Theory for Highly Unsteady Thin Airfoil Motions
papers.abstract: A generalized steady thin airfoil theory is built not from steady flow, but from flows in which there exists a frame of reference where the absolute vorticity field is steady. We specialize this general idea to construct a foliation of a domain of phase space for thin airfoil motions in which staying on a leaf of the foliation maintains zero absolute vorticity in the fluid indefinitely. The phase space is described by the airfoil's total rotation rate, speed, and angle of attack. It is found using this definition that one of the preeminent unsteady stall conditions is equivalent to the traditional steady stall condition for this class of flows, various other classical results can be re-interpreted as steady in the absolute vorticity field, and insight is also provided into the surprising experimental results of McGowan et al. (AIAA J. 49, 2011). We show parts of existing quasi-steady flow and Theodorsen unsteady flow theory can be built from a planar approximation of our foliation, making the quasi-steady extension of our theory trivial, and suggesting how an unsteady extension can be created as well. Furthermore, pure unsteady effects in the new theory amount to a transversal of the leaves, occupying just one dimension, inviting interesting prospects for future experimental and theoretical work.
authors: Scott A. Bollt

papers.title: Boundary spectroscopy of hidden near-horizon reflection
papers.abstract: A classical black hole horizon absorbs completely, and any deviation would be hidden in the bulk. For a scalar field in a rotating Ba\~nados-Teitelboim-Zanelli exterior, we derive an exact boundary response of a corotating passive wall near the horizon. An Airy filter gives its spectrum, and positive energy excludes growing modes. On any frequency band the response identifies a constant wall impedance and the wall position, which enter orthogonally with weights determined by the spectral function. The boundary thus sees a reflecting wall, whereas a perfect absorber is exponentially hidden.
authors: Yiling Chen, Jiayue Yang, Zhen Zhong, Robert B. Mann, Jie Jiang, Ming Zhang

papers.title: Positive-partial-transpose structure of completely entangled subspaces and their complements
papers.abstract: A completely entangled subspace (CES) contains no product vectors, so every state supported on it is entangled. Whether such a subspace can support states with positive partial transpose (PPT) is a more subtle question. The normalized projector onto a CES may be NPT even if there exist PPT states supported on the CES. We investigate this distinction using a semidefinite criterion that optimizes the smallest partial-transpose eigenvalue over all supported density operators. For two- qutrit states supported on CESs, this leads to a complete characterization: a CES supports PPT states exactly when it is four-dimensional and related by invertible local transformations to the complement of an unextendible product basis (UPB). We also establish restrictions on PPT states whose ranges contain only vectors of Schmidt rank at least three, ruling out their existence in $3\otimes n$, $4\otimes4$, and $4\otimes5$, and showing that any such state in $4\otimes6$ must have rank eight. An interesting structure emerges when two orthogonal completely entangled subspaces together span the full Hilbert space, which we term \textit{complementary CESs}. Explicit constructions in $3\otimes4$ demonstrate that both subspaces can support PPT entanglement even when their normalized projectors are NPT. In $4\otimes4$, we construct a complementary pair whose normalized projectors are themselves PPT entangled. These constructions offer an alternative route to obtaining PPT entangled states, beyond the familiar approach based on UPB complements.
authors: Gurvir Singh, Arvind

papers.title: Remote Charging of Quantum Batteries via a Multimode Resonator
papers.abstract: We study the remote charging of a qubit battery by a qubit charger coupled through a finite multimode resonator. The charging protocol uses time-shifted coupling pulses that account for the spatial phases of the resonator modes. We compare the energy stored in the battery with its ergotropy, the maximum work extractable by a local unitary operation. In the single-excitation regime considered here, the battery stores energy at any nonzero excited-state population, but its ergotropy is positive only when that population exceeds one half. In the absence of loss, stronger coupling brings the battery above this threshold earlier, while the final charge remains nearly complete across the coupling range studied. For the parameters considered, qubit relaxation suppresses ergotropy more strongly than resonator loss at comparable decay rates. After the battery is disconnected, relaxation causes its stored energy to decay exponentially, yet its ergotropy vanishes at a finite time while half of its energy capacity remains occupied. For a fixed storage interval, disconnecting at the population maximum therefore preserves the most extractable work.
authors: Maryam Hadipour, Soroush Haseli

papers.title: Diffusivity and metric exponents for slightly supercritical percolation in high dimensions
papers.abstract: It is a classical fact that random walk on the infinite supercritical Bernoulli $p$-percolation cluster on $\mathbb{Z}^{d}$ converges to Brownian motion with some diffusivity $\sigma(p)$, and that the graph metric on the infinite cluster has order $\mu(p) \|\cdot\|$ at large scales for some constant $\mu(p)$ known as the time constant. We compute the near-critical asymptotics of the two quantities in high dimensions, showing that \begin{align*} \sigma^2(p) \asymp (p-p_c)^2 \qquad \text{ and } \qquad \mu(p) \asymp \frac{1}{\sqrt{p-p_c}} \end{align*} for all $p>p_c$. Our results concerning the diffusivity confirm a conjecture of Biskup (2011). We also compute the asymptotic critical probabilities of slabs in the same regime, showing that $p_c( \mathbb{Z}^{d-1} \times \{0,\ldots,n\}) - p_c(\mathbb{Z}^{d}) \asymp n^{-2}$ as $n\to \infty$.
authors: Chenlin Gu, Tom Hutchcroft, Xiaoran Li

papers.title: Quark and gluon gravitational form factors of the nucleon at next-to-leading order
papers.abstract: We compute the quark and gluon gravitational form factors $A$, $J$ and $D$ of the nucleon in three-point QCD sum rules at next-to-leading order in $\alpha_s$ for the quark and gluon energy-momentum tensors (EMT), treating both at the same order in the $\overline{\rm MS}$ scheme. The nucleon EMT also tests the method, showing where the sum rules are reliable and why. Protected estimators of $D$ and of the trace form factor $\bar c$ require antisymmetric Borel moments, since none with equal Borel masses alone is protected. The $\mathcal{O}(\alpha_s)$ corrections reduce $A_{\rm tot}$ by $32$--$40\%$, $J_{\rm tot}$ by $22$--$27\%$ and $|D_{\rm tot}|$ by $21$--$27\%$, since the perturbative share of the two-point function is much larger. The total form factors agree with lattice QCD for $1\le Q^2\le2.5$~GeV$^2$. At $Q^2=1.5$~GeV$^2$, $A_{\rm tot}=0.337\pm0.113$, $J_{\rm tot}=0.206\pm0.100$ and $D_{\rm tot}=-0.206\pm0.121$. $D$ is the most reliable result: its correlator is mostly perturbative, and its quark and gluon parts agree with the lattice. In $A$ and $J$, a local gluon-condensate term that does not fall with $Q^2$ is the largest, and their gluon shares are well below the lattice, possibly because the gluon EMT couples at this order only through gluon exchange and the condensate. A working region exists only near $\beta=1$, and the constant part of transitions cannot be separated within the Borel windows. The individual conservation identities deviate at one point by two standard deviations, consistent with a missing finite term in the $g_{\mu\nu}$ structure, and $\bar c$ is therefore given at leading order with condensates.
authors: Ula\c{s} \"{O}zdem

papers.title: 500 Hz atom-atom entanglement distribution over metropolitan-scale fibers
papers.abstract: Quantum networks and repeaters are among the most promising routes to scale up quantum information systems. Nevertheless, various aspects still require significant improvement to achieve practical realization. Multiplexing can enhance the performance in many fundamental steps, thus emerging as a critical strategy for the realization of quantum repeaters. Currently, a major bottleneck in realizing functional quantum repeaters is heralded entanglement distribution over longdistance elementary links, as neither of the two dominant protocols-single-photon nor two-photon interference-can simultaneously achieve high efficiency and strong robustness. Here, we address this challenge by experimentally realizing a method that unifies the efficiency and robustness. By harnessing two 15 * 15 quantum memory arrays, we generate remote matter-matter entanglement at a rate of 546 Hz over 20 km of fiber without active phase stabilization. This rate exceeds that of two-photon and single-photon schemes by factors of 75,932 and 23, respectively, establishing a new benchmark for entangling speed over metropolitan-scale distances and enabling semi-deterministic entanglement distribution. Inherently compatible with multiplexed quantum repeater architectures, our scheme offers a promising approach towards the realization of future high-performance distributed quantum systems.
authors: Jixuan Shi, Yuedong Sun, Yibo Liang, Sheng Zhang, Pingyuan Liu, Zhaibin Cui, Luming Duan, Yunfei Pu

papers.title: Observable-Level Expressivity in Fixed-Readout Quantum Neural Networks
papers.abstract: A central question in quantum machine learning is which functions of an input state a model can represent when its measurement is fixed by hardware or by experimental design. We address this question for quantum neural networks with a fixed readout observable, where the trainable pre-measurement dynamics determine the effective observable in the Heisenberg picture and the scalar output is the measured expectation value itself, without trainable affine post-processing. We characterize the reachable effective observables under three physical resource classes: unitary evolution, which preserves the spectrum of the readout; mixed-unitary evolution, which relaxes this to a majorization constraint while preserving the trace; and completely positive trace-preserving (CPTP) evolution, whose Heisenberg adjoint is unital rather than trace-preserving and therefore lifts the trace constraint inherited at the mixed-unitary level. The three reachable sets are a fixed-spectrum orbit, its convex hull, and an operator interval, and the inclusions are strict for any readout that is not proportional to the identity. The separation is witnessed locally: for a fixed Pauli readout $Z_j$ on an arbitrary number of qubits, the amplitude-damping observable $\gamma\id+(1-\gamma)Z_j$ lies outside the mixed-unitary level for every $\gamma>0$. We realize the CPTP level with a Stinespring-channelized circuit and derive closed-form loss floors, $4\gamma^2/3$ and $\gamma^2$ for the unitary and mixed-unitary levels and zero at the CPTP level, which the numerics reproduce within precision. Structured-observable, R\'enyi-moment and classification experiments illustrate how the hierarchy manifests in finite-depth ans\"atze. The results identify which spectral constraint each physical resource relaxes, framing reachable-observable classes as a resource for expressivity rather than an architectural advantage.
authors: Iqra Bashir, Yuanfeng Wang, Mingda Huang, Keren Li, Qi Qin

papers.title: Quantum simulation of low-temperature impurity models
papers.abstract: Quantum impurity models, which describe a small but strongly-interacting subsystem coupled to a large noninteracting bath, are the computational core of dynamical mean field theory and play an important role in simulating strongly correlated materials. We develop quantum algorithms for efficiently simulating these models at low temperatures and with high precision. For any impurity model on $n$ fermionic modes with fixed impurity size: (1) We give a quantum algorithm that prepares the thermal state at inverse temperature $\beta$ to precision $\delta$ in time $\mathrm{poly}(n,\beta,\log(1/\delta))$. This algorithm is the first to achieve both polynomial scaling in the inverse temperature and polylogarithmic scaling in the precision. When the Hamiltonian has an inverse-polynomial spectral gap, our quantum algorithm prepares its ground state to precision $\delta$ in time $\mathrm{poly}(n,\log(1/\delta))$. (2) We further give a quantum algorithm that prepares a purification of the thermal state in time $\mathrm{poly}(n,\beta,\log(1/\delta))$. Using this purification, we estimate static and dynamical properties with error $\delta$ in time polynomial in $n$ and $\beta$ and linear in $1/\delta$ up to polylogarithmic factors, achieving the Heisenberg scaling. Our algorithms build on quantum Gibbs samplers, which are quantum analogues of Markov chain Monte Carlo methods. By using global jump operators instead of local ones, we avoid the $\exp(\beta)$ overhead commonly associated with quantum Gibbs samplers, making them efficient for impurity models even at low temperatures.
authors: Jiaqing Jiang, Nathan Ju

papers.title: Combining Schr\"odinger and Heisenberg Evolution to Extend Quantum Many-Body Simulations
papers.abstract: Classical simulations of quantum many-body dynamics face complementary limitations: entanglement growth restricts state evolution in the Schr\"odinger picture, while operator spreading makes Heisenberg-picture calculations increasingly expensive. Here, we combine both approaches by evolving quantum states and observables independently and joining their dynamics through massively parallel tensor-network contractions. We implement this strategy using tree tensor networks and sparse Pauli propagation, extending evolution times beyond those reached by either method separately in our calculations. For a quench of the two-dimensional transverse-field Ising model at the critical field, we simulate the magnetization of an $11\times11$ open lattice up to $t=1.20$ by combining state and operator evolution over intervals $t_S=t_H=0.60$. We compare the dynamics with iPEPS, numerical linked-cluster expansion, and X-truncated sparse Pauli dynamics results. We also combine exact state evolution on small clusters with operator propagation on a larger lattice, improving agreement with iPEPS relative to cluster evolution alone. We further derive error bounds showing how the state can suppress operator errors and the evolved observable can reduce sensitivity to state errors.
authors: Zhigang Hu, Igor Ermakov, Yauheni Talochka, Biao Wu, Oleg Lychkovskiy

papers.title: Quantum Subentropy: Subadditivity and Sharp Bounds on Discrimination Error
papers.abstract: Subentropy gives a tight spectral lower bound on the accessible information of ensembles of pure states. We prove its subadditivity for arbitrary bipartite states in finite dimensions and derive a sharp relation between conditional subentropy and the minimum discrimination error. This relation strengthens a conjectured comparison with conditional min-entropy. Its inverse gives the strongest universal lower bound on the error determined only by conditional subentropy and the number of labels. Both main results follow from a comparison of conditional subentropy with the average subentropy of measurement posteriors, valid for mixed signal states and every finite measurement. We characterize all equality cases in these two results and bound posterior deviations near equality. We also determine the optimal Lipschitz constant in trace distance for conditional subentropy on classical-quantum states, including the exact constant when the quantum marginal is fixed. A determinant inequality strengthens subadditivity and proves strong subadditivity for classical distributions, while an exact counterexample shows that strong subadditivity fails for quantum states. Lean 4 proofs of all theoretical results are available at https://pratikpatil.io/lean/subentropy/
authors: Pratik Patil

papers.title: Charged spin-$\frac32$ in a chiral Feshbach--Villars model: hyperbolic propagation, Landau-level instability, and exceptional points
papers.abstract: We study a Pauli-coupled second-order wave equation on $(\frac32,0)\oplus(0,\frac32)$ with a free gyromagnetic ratio $g$. Its Feshbach--Villars form is a sixteen-component pseudo-Hermitian Hamiltonian system with lightlike covariant characteristics in smooth electromagnetic backgrounds. The solution space is chirality doubled; a covariant physical single-species reduction is not assumed. The exact spin-$j$ Landau spectrum remains real at every field strength precisely when $|g|j\le1$. At $g=2$, the critical spin-$\frac32$ channel reaches zero at $|qB|=m^2/2$, where each chiral block develops a second-order exceptional point. This threshold also marks the loss of a time-independent positive-definite conserved quadratic form for the channel. We also include a bounded, Gaussian-damped harmonic electrostatic potential and its associated electric field. The complete first-order problem on a degenerate manifold reduces to $V\pm iC$, with $V$ and $C$ the projected potential and spin--electric coupling. On the lowest two-state spin-$\frac32$ manifold, nonreal eigenvalue branches arise for $m^2/6<|qB|<m^2/2$ at sufficiently small nonzero perturbation amplitude, except at a special well range where the first-order splitting vanishes. The spin-$\frac12$, $g=2$ limit satisfies the Dirac spectral-reality check, whereas $g=1/j$ has no imaginary first-order correction for this perturbation. These results separate spectral instability from loss of hyperbolicity; they do not establish a physical fermionic quantization.
authors: Haryanto M. Siahaan

papers.title: Rank-Two Attractors and Modularity for a Mirror Bicubic
papers.abstract: We study the mirror family $\mathcal X_\lambda$ of the bicubic Calabi-Yau threefold, obtained from a family of complete intersections of two cubics in $\mathbb P^5$. We show that the four-dimensional weight-three Hodge structure of the fibers over $\lambda^6 = -8$ splits into two rational rank-two pieces of Hodge types $(1,0,0,1)$ and $(0,1,1,0)$; in particular, these points are rank-two attractor points. Using a Hesse pencil fiber-product realization, equivariant point counting, and the Serre-Faltings-Livne method, we identify their semisimplified $\ell$-adic Galois representations with those attached to the weight-four newform $f_{\mathsf{54.4.a.c}}$ and the Tate twist of the weight-two newform $f_{\mathsf{54.2.a.a}}$, where these labels refer to the L-functions and modular forms database.
authors: Yibing Chen, Emanuel Scheidegger

papers.title: The type-II double copy for relativistic Rindler fluids
papers.abstract: Within the Weyl double copy framework, we study a mixed single-copy construction for the Petrov type-II geometry of first-order relativistic Rindler fluids. Working on a common fixed flat Rindler background with consistent spinor conventions and a real field strength representation, we algebraically factorize the Weyl spinor into two symmetric rank-two Maxwell spinors and test the Maxwell equations and the zeroth copy scalar equation up to the first order in the relativistic gradient expansion. We separate the degeneration parameter from the gradient expansion parameter and analyze the continuous degeneration to the Petrov type-D and type-N branches as the complex shear and vorticity tend to zero, together with the preservation of the accuracy of the Maxwell and scalar field equations along each path. We also compare the relativistic construction with the nonrelativistic case.
authors: Yu-Cheng Wang, Jing-Rui Zhang, Yun-Long Zhang

papers.title: Privacy-Enhanced Distributed Sensing Network via Causal-Order Switching and Probe Squeezing
papers.abstract: As sensor networks become more interconnected, sensitive information sharing among multiple users poses potential risks of information leakage, making privacy protection a critical challenge. To address this challenge, we quantify network privacy using the maximum information leakage ratio (MILR) and propose a protocol that enhances privacy through causal-order switching and probe squeezing. Causal-order switching harnesses intrinsic network propagation dynamics for privacy encoding, while probe squeezing suppresses information leakage through quantum channels and increases the information available for estimating the global parameter. These mechanisms enable an asymptotic exponential enhancement on the privacy with the squeezing rate. We experimentally demonstrate this mechanism in distributed beam-tilt sensing using spatially structured light without requiring nonclassical light sources. Our work identifies intrinsic network propagation dynamics as a resource for privacy protection and opens a new avenue for continuous-variable sensing networks that combine high precision with enhanced privacy.
authors: Zhaotong Cui, Binke Xia, Yuxiang Yang, Hongjing Li, Jingzheng Huang, Guihua Zeng

papers.title: A note on Kaluza-Klein theories
papers.abstract: We present a variant of the Kaluza-Klein theory that was introduced in previous papers (ATMP, 2020; LMP 2022; Ann. Fac. Sci. Toulouse, 2025), based on an action functional whose critical points, in the presence of point-wise constraints, lead-under reasonable assumptions-to the existence of a principal fiber bundle and solutions to the Einstein-Yang-Mills system. The difference is that it is not necessary to impose a point-wise constraint.
authors: Fr{\'e}d{\'e}ric H{\'e}lein (IMJ-PRG)

papers.title: Matter-decorated trumpets in double-scaled SYK
papers.abstract: In sine-dilaton gravity, the double trumpet, the wormhole amplitude without matter, is obtained by gluing two trumpets along a closed geodesic of discrete length and summing over this length. When the wormhole carries the propagator of a matter field of dimension $\Delta$, joining the two asymptotic boundaries and crossing the neck, such a gluing is known only in the Jackiw--Teitelboim (JT) limit. We construct the gluing beyond JT in double-scaled SYK (DSSYK), the proposed boundary dual of sine-dilaton gravity, whose disk amplitudes it reproduces. In this context, we adopt the definition of the matter-decorated wormhole in terms of the ETH two-matrix model with Gaussian matter. We build matter-decorated trumpets from an end-of-the-world brane trace with a matter insertion, and prove that the wormhole is glued from them exactly, sector by sector in the number of chords through the neck, with a positive weight that accounts for the twists and windings of these chords and for the closed loops around the neck. Trumpets and weight are obtained in closed form, the former as transforms of Rogers polynomials, and we discuss the uniqueness of the construction. In the JT limit, both reproduce the known gluing separately, and not only in combination. In the classical limit, each trumpet takes the form expected in the bulk: a pure-gravity sine-dilaton trumpet dressed by the factor that a probe matter geodesic contributes at its boundary.
authors: Matteo Beccaria

papers.title: Impact of structured noise on bosonic quantum error correction
papers.abstract: Bosonic quantum error correction relies on an accurate description of single-photon loss dissipation using an ideal annihilation operator, under which correctable loss errors act equivalently on different logical code states. In realistic weakly nonlinear bosonic modes, however, coupling to a structured environment can render photon loss Fock-state dependent, thereby modifying the effective dissipation operator and deforming the associated error space. Here, we experimentally investigate this effect in a three-dimensional circuit quantum electrodynamics system. By injecting spectrally engineered environmental noise into a weakly nonlinear oscillator, we observe pronounced frequency selectivity in the measured Fock-state dynamics. While the long-time transition rates converge to the Markovian limit, the transient dynamics display distinctly non-Markovian behavior, in quantitative agreement with a second-order time-convolutionless theory. By applying narrowband noise to a binomially encoded logical qubit, we further demonstrate Fock-state-dependent dissipation channels that drive logical states beyond the nominally correctable error space. These results establish structured environmental noise as a mechanism for deforming photon-loss errors in weakly nonlinear bosonic systems and highlight the need to incorporate realistic, state-dependent dissipation into the design and characterization of bosonic quantum error correction.
authors: Guoyu Shu, Ling Hu, Hongbo Wu, Zhongchu Ni, Yanyan Cai, Xiaowei Deng, Pan Zheng, Pengbo Li, Fei Yan, Song Liu, Dapeng Yu, Yuan Xu

papers.title: Dark matter mass fraction in axion stars
papers.abstract: QCD axion dark matter is fragmented into small mass miniclusters of high density. With the natural parameters of miniclusters, the time for Bose-Einstein condensation is less than the age of the Universe, which leads to the formation of Bose stars inside these structures. Recently, the problem of the subsequent growth of Bose stars was solved analytically (Dmitriev et al, Phys. Rev. Lett. 132, 091001 (2024)). We use this solution to determine present day mass fraction of dark matter in Bose stars and their mass function.
authors: A. S. Dmitriev, D. G. Levkov, A. G. Panin, I. I. Tkachev

papers.title: Rotating Black Holes from Scaling Transformations in Horava Gravity
papers.abstract: We study the scaling transformations that change the physical parameters of solutions in low-energy Horava gravity. In particular, we present a simple scaling transformation that generates rotating black-hole solutions in low-energy Horava gravity from known relativistic solutions. As explicit examples, we obtain "Doran-like" and "Kerr-Schild-like" rotating solutions in Horava gravity. We find that both solutions are horizon-penetrating, but their null horizons are not Killing horizons. We also find that, although their singularity structures differ from each other, chronology is protected in both solutions, as in the previously obtained Kerr-like solutions in Boyer-Lindquist coordinates.
authors: Deniz O. Devecioglu, Mu-In Park

papers.title: Derivation of BCS functionals and gap equations from quantum many-body fermionic system
papers.abstract: We consider 3D single-species spin-$1/2$ Fermi systems with general dispersion relation and general attractive interaction initially inside a finite box. Up to some critical temperature $T_c$ determined by the interaction and system size, we establish, for the expected discrete BCS gap equation, existence of positive maximal solution. We then prove the uniqueness of nonzero (not identically zero) nonnegative solution. That is, any nonzero nonnegative solution, if exist or obtained via other methods, must equal to the positive maximal solution. Building on such a well-posedness result and assuming quasi-freeness, we prove the emergence of the $SU(2)$ symmetry of the finite system. Finally, letting the system size tend to infinity, we prove the emergence of the continuous BCS functional and gap equation for which we also have the uniqueness of nonzero nonnegative solution, and the convergence of the critical temperature. In particular, our work also implies there is a positive energy (hence mass) gap for aforementioned Fermi systems for $[0,T_c)$, any nonzero nonnegative solution for the gap equations are from the many-body system it suppose to describe, and the Cooper divergence of the density of states from a finite to an infinite system.
authors: Xuwen Chen, Jiahao Wu, Zhifei Zhang

papers.title: Critical Topology: A New Perspective for Phase Transitions
papers.abstract: Critical topology has emerged as a form of quantum criticality beyond the Landau paradigm, challenging conventional approaches to classifying universality classes by introducing topological properties as an additional criterion. Despite substantial progress over the past five years, several fundamental questions remain open. Theoretically, can we establish a general criterion for the emergence of critical topology? Can a unified theoretical framework be extended beyond one-dimensional quantum many-body systems? What efficient numerical methods can be developed to investigate critical topological states in higher-dimensional strongly correlated systems? Experimentally, research has so far focused primarily on single-particle critical topology. An important next step is to realize and characterize many-body critical topology in quantum systems using platforms such as Rydberg atom arrays, superconducting quantum processors, and quantum materials. Major advances in statistical physics often arise from re-examining fundamental concepts. The theory of critical phenomena developed by Landau, Ginzburg, and Wilson, together with the topological phase transitions pioneered by Kosterlitz and Thouless, has now inspired new discoveries in artificial acoustic metamaterials. These experimental observations mark a beginning rather than an endpoint for research on critical topology, and further advances in this direction are anticipated.
authors: Xue-Jia Yu

papers.title: Imprints of quantum space in the ringdown phase of Kerr black holes
papers.abstract: We investigate quantum-space corrections to the gravitational quasinormal modes (QNMs) of Kerr black holes within the framework of noncommutative geometry. The analysis employs a pseudo-semi-Killing Drinfeld twist, which preserves the classical Kerr geometry as an exact background solution while introducing nontrivial quantum corrections to linearized gravitational perturbations. Working to first order in the black hole spin and the quantum deformation parameter, including their mixed contribution, we derive a Schr\"odinger-like master equation for axial gravitational perturbations with a frequency- and spin-dependent effective potential. We compute the fundamental QNM frequencies using the WKB approximation and Leaver's continued-fraction method.Our results reveal corrections to the QNM oscillation frequencies and damping rates arising from rotation, pure quantum effects, and their interplay.To the best of our knowledge, this is the first systematic analysis of gravitational metric perturbations in a noncommutative Kerr black hole spacetime using a Drinfeld twist, extending prior work beyond the Schwarzschild case. Our findings demonstrate that quantum deformation effects alter both the oscillation frequencies and damping rates of quasinormal modes, with spin-quantum coupling introducing additional spin-dependent corrections to the Kerr QNM spectrum. Using a Kerr-anchored phenomenological prescription, we estimate the fractional frequency and damping-time shifts for selected merger remnants from the GWTC-3 and GWTC-5.0 catalogs. These estimates illustrate the potential signatures of quantum corrections in gravitational-wave ringdown.
authors: Nikola Herceg, Tajron Juri\'c, A. Naveena Kumara, Andjelo Samsarov, Ivica Smoli\'c, Kumar S. Gupta

papers.title: Quantum walks and conformal mappings
papers.abstract: We study the most elementary discrete model of an electron moving along a line, known as Feynman checkers, quantum walk, or the six-vertex model with special complex weights, and provide a uniform asymptotic formula for the wave function in the whole xt-plane. In addition to the well-known appearance of the Airy function that describes the transition between the oscillating and exponentially decaying regimes, we observe a second transition governed by the gamma function when the electron speed approaches the speed of light. We prove two general theorems producing uniform asymptotic formulae involving the Airy and gamma functions, using conformal mappings associated with the underlying integral representations. They are applicable in several other situations as well.
authors: Fedor Kuyanov, Michael Drmota, Mikhail Skopenkov, Alexey Ustinov

papers.title: Universal thermodynamics and BKT transition of the planar Bose gas from weak to strong interactions
papers.abstract: We compute the universal thermodynamics of the dilute two-dimensional Bose gas at weak and strong coupling using the functional renormalization group (FRG). We employ an approximation that retains the full field dependence of the effective potential and spatial derivative terms, extending previous FRG calculations. We find that the equation of state is remarkably insensitive to the approximation scheme, with differences of only a few percent even at strong coupling. By contrast, the improved approximation substantially improves the description of the Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless (BKT) transition, reproducing the universal jump of the superfluid density and the critical anomalous dimension to within a few percent. At weak coupling, our results agree very well with classical-field Monte Carlo simulations, while at stronger coupling we observe deviations from classical-field scaling, valid at weak coupling. Our approach thus provides a quantitative description of the thermodynamics and superfluid density across the BKT transition, including in the strong-coupling regime where classical-field methods are no longer reliable.
authors: Yaniss Rabahi, Ivan Balog, Adam Ran\c{c}on

papers.title: Uniform Ionization Bounds in Molecular Thomas--Fermi--Dirac--von Weizs\"acker Theory
papers.abstract: We study the molecular Thomas--Fermi--Dirac--von Weizs\"acker theory. For each fixed number $K$ of nuclei, we prove that every minimizer of mass $N$ satisfies $N\leq Z+C_K$, where $Z$ is the total nuclear charge, and $C_K>0$ is independent of the nuclear charges and positions. This answers the molecular large-charge ionization question posed in [R. L. Frank, P. T. Nam and H. Van Den Bosch, CPAM, 2018]. For $N\geq Z$, we also compare the screened potentials and electronic radii of Thomas--Fermi--Dirac--von Weizs\"acker minimizers with those of the corresponding neutral molecular Thomas--Fermi minimizers and establish a uniform bound on the ionization energy.
authors: Shuang Wu

papers.title: Confidence-Aware Discriminative Readout of Neutral-Atom Arrays
papers.abstract: Fast and reliable detection is a central requirement for neutral atom quantum computers, yet fluorescence imaging remains a limiting step for rapid experimental cycling, large-scale array operation, and quantum-error-correction protocols. In this work, we demonstrate confidence-aware readout of $^{171}\mathrm{Yb}$ atoms in optical tweezers using a discriminative classifier. Rather than forcing each atom-site image directly into a hard binary outcome, the proposed readout produces a measurement reliability score. This score is produced by a logistic-regression classifier trained on features derived from both the total photon count and the spatial pattern of fluorescence at each site. The resulting classifier achieves the same readout fidelity with approximately half the imaging time. At an exposure of 10 ms, it achieves $99.83\%$ readout fidelity, comparable to the $99.82\%$ achieved by conventional photon-count thresholding at 20 ms. Importantly, the classifier score enables low-confidence outcomes to be converted into measurement-level erasures, leaving fewer residual unflagged errors at a fixed erasure budget. This improvement is further accompanied by strong false-positive suppression, which is important for downstream operations such as atom rearrangement where false positives can create target defects. Monte Carlo rearrangement simulations show that the reduced false-positive rate and confidence-based erasure conversion improve predicted defect-free assembly performance. This work establishes confidence-aware readout using a discriminative classifier as a practical paradigm for fast and scalable neutral-atom quantum computing.
authors: Jaeick Bae, Kangheun Kim, Yunheung Song, Junseo Ha, Jeong Ho Han, Jaewook Ahn, Hyunsoo Ha, Soonwon Choi, Jongchul Mun

papers.title: Non-Perturbative Analysis of Resonances by a Contraction Mapping on Complex Domains
papers.abstract: In this paper, we consider a perturbation problem of embedded eigenvalues for an abstract Friedrichs--Lee Hamiltonian and analyze its spectral properties. By deforming the contour and constructing a contraction mapping on complex domains, we prove the existence of resonance poles.
authors: Toshimitsu Takaesu, Tamotsu Teruya

papers.title: Exact finite-sample and loss limits of squeezed-vacuum phase estimation
papers.abstract: We settle the dispute over squeezed-vacuum phase estimation by exact computation of the finite-sample errors, resource-fair scaling, phase window, and loss ceilings. A fixed overhead of ten repetitions sets the attainable finite-sample frontier; the repetitions cancel from the resource-fair bound, so Heisenberg scaling survives; the operating window holds a repetition-set number of resolvable points and needs one bit of branch prior; and fixed loss caps the per-photon advantage at a value set only by transmissivity, already reached by the reported record.
authors: Wangjun Lu, Qing Yu

papers.title: Darboux transformation for the ASDYM equations: Solitons and instantons
papers.abstract: Using a one-fold Darboux transformation for the anti-self-dual Yang--Mills equations, we express the Yang--Mills Lagrangian density in terms of $\tau$-functions. For solitons constructed from exponential functions, we show that the associated $\tau$-functions admit a parametrization by arbitrary points in the Grassmannian Gr(N,M;$\mathbb{C}$), and construct the corresponding Yang--Mills fields. For instantons arising from the Atiyah--Drinfeld--Hitchin--Manin (ADHM) construction, we reinterpret the ADHM construction in terms of a one-fold Darboux transformation, recover Osborn's formula for the Yang--Mills Lagrangian density, and obtain the corresponding gauge connection.
authors: Shangshuai Li

papers.title: Liouvillian Quasiparticle Spectroscopy
papers.abstract: Quasiparticles play a central role in understanding closed quantum many-body systems, as they reduce complex many-body problems to effective single-particle descriptions and connect directly to spectroscopic measurements. In open quantum systems, the interplay between coherent dynamics and dissipation gives rise to unique phenomena, such as the Liouvillian skin effect and strong-to-weak spontaneous symmetry breaking. This raises a fundamental question: how can the quasiparticle picture be extended to open quantum systems to account for such phenomena and enable the experimental probing of quasiparticle spectra? Here we introduce coherent and incoherent Liouvillian quasiparticles, defined by responses to perturbations acting on one side and both sides of the density matrix, respectively. We propose spectroscopy protocols that couple the system to auxiliary levels, either coherently or via a dissipative pulse, to measure the corresponding complex quasiparticle energies. Numerical simulations of Liouvillians with skin effects validate these protocols, revealing nontrivial spectral winding associated with unidirectional transport in real space. Notably, coherent and incoherent quasiparticles can propagate in opposite directions within the same system. Furthermore, in models exhibiting weak and strong-to-weak $U(1)$ spontaneous symmetry breaking, our results unveil gapless Nambu-Goldstone modes in the coherent and incoherent quasiparticle spectra, respectively; the other quasiparticle spectrum remains gapped in each case. Our work provides a unified framework for theoretically describing and experimentally probing coherent and incoherent quasiparticles in open quantum many-body systems.
authors: Kai Li, Masahito Ueda

papers.title: Dissipative Tidal Love Numbers of Neutron Stars from Viscous Heating
papers.abstract: We compute the leading low-frequency dissipative tidal response of nonrotating relativistic neutron stars. We formulate the response in a worldline effective field theory. We determine the linear dissipative Love number in two complementary ways: from the redshifted viscous entropy production inside the star and from the imaginary, frequency-odd part of the exterior metric. The first method reduces the calculation to an integral over the static equilibrium tide; the second provides an independent check. We apply our approach to publicly available equations of state and assess the corresponding correction to the gravitational-wave phase of neutron-star binaries. For an equal-mass $1.4+1.4M_\odot$ binary with both stars at a redshifted temperature $T_\infty=10^5\,\mathrm K$ and a standard electron shear viscosity, tidal dissipation shifts the gravitational-wave phase by less than $10^{-3}$ cycles between $20\,{\rm Hz}$ and $1\,{\rm kHz}$ for the four equations of state considered. Including the resulting rise in the stars' temperature in a simple thermal model reduces the shift below $10^{-6}$ cycles. For the viscosity model considered here, shear-viscous tidal dissipation in cold neutron stars is negligible for gravitational-wave phasing. This suggests that a measurable dissipative tidal signature would have to come from a different mechanism.
authors: Nikola Savi\'c, Filippo Vernizzi

papers.title: For whom the Bell tolls: joint measurements and state updates in quantum field theory
papers.abstract: State update rules and their behaviour in Bell tests play an important role in the study of measurement schemes and quantum information. We consider the state updates of the Fewster-Verch measurement framework for quantum field theory using their connection to the probability distribution of measurement outcomes. We focus on a set of observables of the form $A(f_i)^*A(f_i)$, where $A(f)$ is the (complex) smeared field operator for any theory induced by a formally hermitian, Green hyperbolic differential operator, and where the $(A(f_i))_{i=1, \dots, m}$ are assumed to be normal and mutually commuting. Under the assumption that these operators have a sufficiently nice representation on a bosonic Fock space, we derive the joint moment generating functional and the unique joint probability distribution for the observables $(A(f_i)^*A(f_i))_{i=1,\dots,m}$. As an application of these results, we construct a model of a Bell inequality test within quantum field theory using a recently developed coupled Proca-scalar model for polarization measurements. We show that our Bell test model can violate the CHSH inequality, approaching Tsirelson's bound for maximally entangled states in the limit where vacuum effects are perfectly rejected. These results show that the state update rules derived in the Fewster-Verch framework are compatible with strongly quantum correlations. They also support a viewpoint in which state updates should be understood in relation to available information.
authors: Christopher J. Fewster, Christiane K. M. Klein

papers.title: Exact solution of the long-range voter model in arbitrary dimensions: correlations and effective-dimensional scaling
papers.abstract: Long-range interactions can profoundly alter collective ordering and critical behavior, yet exact ana- lytical results for non-equilibrium systems with such interactions remain scarce. We obtain an exact analytical solution for the spatial correlation function of the voter model with long-range interac- tions in arbitrary spatial dimension. Starting from the evolution equation for the Fourier modes, we identify the long-wavelength dispersion generated by the interaction kernel and derive the resulting coarsening and stationary scaling regimes. The solution yields the critical condition separating these regimes, the characteristic coarsening length, and the asymptotic decay of stationary correlations. These results establish an exact effective-dimensional correspondence: the long-range model in dimen- sion d, with interaction exponent \b{eta}, exhibits the same scaling exponents as a short-range voter model in the effective dimension deff = 2d/\b{eta}. The correspondence holds across the coarsening, marginal, and stationary regimes, while the associated scaling functions need not coincide
authors: Fabrizio Rippa, Jacopo Alexander Garofalo, Giuseppe Petrillo, Eugenio Lippiello

papers.title: Pion scattering in finite volume within the Inverse Amplitude Method: Extension to moving frames
papers.abstract: We study the leading exponentially suppressed finite-volume corrections to $\pi\pi$ scattering near threshold in moving frames. Using the one-loop Inverse Amplitude Method (IAM), we compute the $I=0$ and $I=2$ amplitudes in a box with total momentum $\vec P=2\pi\vec d/L$, including the left-hand cut and the $t$-, $u$-channel and tadpole contributions neglected in L\"uscher's quantization condition. We derive the resulting correction to the near-threshold energy levels and measure its size relative to the L\"uscher term. We find that it becomes comparable to the latter for $m_\pi L\lesssim 1.5$--$1.7$ at rest, and that it is larger in moving frames, reaching $m_\pi L\lesssim 2.8$ for $\vec d=[002]$. The corrections become negligible only for $m_\pi L\gtrsim 5$.
authors: Juli\'an A. S\'anchez, Raquel Molina, \'Angel G\'omez Nicola

papers.title: Universal stabilizer correlations in chaotic eigenstates
papers.abstract: Entanglement and nonstabilizerness provide complementary perspectives on quantum-state structure. In this work, we find that the stabilizer correlation, defined as the difference between the R\'enyi-$2$ mutual information and the mutual stabilizer R\'enyi entropy, approaches a universal constant for chaotic eigenstates. This constant is determined solely by the symmetries, and quantifies the correlation that does not contribute to nonstabilizerness. We identify this universal stabilizer correlation analytically via random-state ensembles, which give $\log_2 7$ (GOE) and $\log_2 4$(GUE) without extra symmetries, $\log_2 14$ and $\log_2 8$ under spin-inversion parity or half-filling magnetization. While imposing reflection or translation symmetry leaves these values unchanged. Exact calculations for a chaotic mixed-field Ising chain confirm the predicted plateau and finite-size approach. Integrable free-fermion and strongly disordered eigenstates behave qualitatively differently. This universal stabilizer correlation reveals a characteristic structure of chaotic eigenstates beyond entanglement or nonstabilizerness alone.
authors: Zhi-Han Liu, Hao-Yue Qi, Wei Zheng

papers.title: Constraints on ultralight dark matter couplings from orbital perturbations of binary pulsars
papers.abstract: Ultralight dark matter coupled directly to ordinary matter perturbs the orbits of binary pulsars, and the perturbation grows secularly when its frequency matches a harmonic of the orbital motion. We use this effect to constrain three couplings with the wideband timing data for the $50$ binary pulsars of the NANOGrav 15 yr data set: a linear and a quadratic universal coupling of a scalar field to matter, and a vector field coupled to baryon minus lepton number ($B-L$). For every system and for masses between $10^{-23}$ and $10^{-18}\,$eV, we build the timing signature from the perturbed orbital elements. We then sample the coupling together with the local amplitude, phase and direction of the field and the red noise of the pulsar, marginalizing analytically over the timing model, and combine the single-pulsar likelihoods into $95\%$ credible upper limits at each mass. For a universal linear coupling, the orbital resonances of the eccentric systems bring the limit close to the Cassini bound. For the quadratic coupling, treating the neutron star as a point particle, the limits are the strongest available between $2\times10^{-22}$ and $2\times10^{-21}\,$eV. In the case of vector ultralight dark matter, the limit is comparable to the PPTA and E\"ot-Wash bounds between $3\times10^{-22}$ and $10^{-21}\,$eV and reaches or beats the E\"ot-Wash bound at isolated orbital resonances, while MICROSCOPE remains stronger over the entire mass range.
authors: Federico Huxhagen, Diana L\'opez Nacir

papers.title: Non-invertible Duality Defects in Four-Dimensional $\mathbb{Z}_N$ Lattice Gauge Theories
papers.abstract: We consider four-dimensional $\mathbb{Z}_N$ lattice gauge theories with generalized plaquette actions. These theories are known to exhibit dualities. We construct topological interfaces implementing these dualities by assigning a weight to each building block and proving topological invariance. At self-dual couplings, these interfaces become duality defects representing non-invertible symmetries. We also study center symmetry defects and their junctions with the duality interfaces and derive several crossing relations.
authors: Satoshi Yamaguchi

papers.title: Progress on finite temperature Sp(4) lattice gauge theory with matter fields
papers.abstract: We explore the finite temperature behaviour of the Sp(4) lattice gauge theory coupled to two dynamical Wilson fermions transforming in the fundamental representation. The continuum theory provides a realisation of composite dark matter within the Strongly Interacting Massive Particle (SIMP) paradigm. Its thermal phase transition in the early universe might have generated an observable relic stochastic gravitational wave signal. Evaluating the sensitivity of future gravitational wave experiments to this signal requires knowledge of the strength of the phase transition. We explore the two dimensional parameter space of the theory, defined by the bare fermion mass and inverse gauge coupling. For this exploratory study we focus on lattices with a small number of sites in the temporal dimension. We analyse the finite volume scaling behaviour of Polyakov loop observables. Specifically the scaling of the peak of the susceptibility, informed by multiple histogram reweighting, is used to discriminate between the presence of a phase transition or crossover. In the light fermion mass regime we find strong indications of a crossover, while for heavy fermions we find preliminary evidence of a first-order phase transition. These findings motivate further studies of the continuum limit for this and other Sp(2N) gauge theories.
authors: Alexis Verney-Provatas, Chris Allton, Ed Bennett, Luigi Del Debbio, Ryan C. Hill, Deog Ki Hong, Jong-Wan Lee, C. -J. David Lin, Biagio Lucini, Maurizio Piai, Davide Vadacchino

papers.title: Binary-Tree Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm for the Maximum $k$-Cut Problem
papers.abstract: The maximum $k$-cut (Max-$k$-Cut) problem, as a natural generalization of the maximum-cut (MaxCut) problem, has broader applications in practical engineering. To solve this problem on quantum devices, existing studies typically encode the $k$ possible subset assignments of each vertex within the quantum approximate optimization algorithm (QAOA), which directly causes the required quantum resources to grow substantially with $k$. Here we propose a binary-tree quantum approximate optimization algorithm (BT-QAOA), which solves the Max-$k$-Cut problem by applying standard MaxCut QAOA to at most $2k-3$ subproblems. Specifically, after solving MaxCut once on the full vertex set, each subsequent step splits only the subset that yields the largest cut-value gain. This process is equivalent to constructing a binary tree whose leaf nodes after $k-1$ steps form an approximate solution to the Max-$k$-Cut problem. Furthermore, we derive a theoretical lower bound on the approximation ratio in terms of the single-step splitting quality, showing that the overall approximation ratio does not decay exponentially across multiple splits. Numerical simulations show that BT-QAOA substantially reduces the single-circuit qubit and gate overhead while maintaining a high approximation ratio, improving the estimated success probability of a single compiled circuit by orders of magnitude. This work effectively expands the practical reach of QAOA on near-term quantum hardware, offering a new route for solving more complex real-world optimization problems with limited quantum resources.
authors: Zhaoyang Song, Wei Zhang, Ji Cao, Xuexi Yi, Hong-Fu Wang

papers.title: Collective order from language models without communication, memory or shared context
papers.abstract: Physical matter orders without a centre: units interact only with neighbours, and fluctuations carry them over energy barriers from a locally stable arrangement to the ordered state. We ask whether language-model agents can do the same, treating each memoryless query as a particle that sees its neighbours but cannot communicate, has no identifier or shared context and receives the same question as all others. Such a particle behaves as if at zero temperature: told a rule or a temperature, it returns the most probable state, and a collective can freeze in a local minimum. We therefore give each particle only a goal and a die whose weights it sets itself, and test several models. Some of them use the die as a noise source even at a local optimum, with weights that fall with the energy cost of the move; on a lattice the energy of one of them climbs over barriers and reaches the ground state, where the noise stops by itself. Particles in three-lane counterflow also order, from mixed traffic into one-way lanes: a spontaneous symmetry breaking. Decentralized collective order can thus arise from disorder without communication, memory or shared context, with noise that the particles choose themselves.
authors: Yong Wang

papers.title: Nonequilibrium Dynamics of R-loop Formation in the CRISPR-Cas9 System
papers.abstract: The binding specificity of CRISPR-Cas9 is governed by the stepwise formation of an R-loop, in which the sgRNA displaces the nontarget DNA strand and hybridizes with the target strand in discrete base pair steps. Here we develop a nonequilibrium dynamics framework that models R-loop formation as a continuous-time Markov birth-death process over twenty base pairs. Each transition rate is derived from Eyring transition-state theory and the Bell model, and combines three physical contributions, i.e., the torsional strain generated by the B-form to A-form helical conversion at the unwinding front, a base stacking correction that couples neighboring base pairs, and the allosteric work supplied by Cas9 conformational changes. We further derive the entropy production of the process, which is decomposed into activation, stacking, torsional, and allosteric terms. The resulting prediction model uses no external thermodynamic database and reaches Spearman correlations of 0.84 and 0.82 in two independent libraries of dCas9-sgRNA mismatch variants measured in vivo. The mismatch-type dependence is carried by one twist deviation and one pairing weight per type. Our model recovers the seed region sensitivity, the PAM-proximal activity gradient, and the moderate cost of dDrG mismatches, while isolating the high-activity double mismatch tail as the regime in which the present free-energy mapping is inadequate. The framework gives quantitative predictions on how DNA supercoiling and sequence context modulate binding affinity, and provides a mechanistic basis for sgRNA design.
authors: Yu Liu, Bing Miao

papers.title: Density of states for random Schr\"odinger operators with linearly correlated heavy-tailed disorder
papers.abstract: We study the density of states of random Schr\"odinger operators with linearly correlated heavy-tailed disorder. Using an integration-by-parts supersymmetric representation, we prove smoothness of the density of states and Wegner estimates in the strong-disorder regime. We are particularly interested in mixed-sign correlation kernels, which serve as a toy model for the hyperbolic structures arising in the analysis of averaged squared Green's functions. Our approach applies to a broad class of correlation kernels and disorder distributions, including $\alpha$-stable laws.
authors: Margherita Disertori, Luca Fresta, Liza Schonlau

papers.title: Chiral crossover responses in a magnetic field: Finite-$\mu_5$ matching in the NJL model
papers.abstract: We investigate how independent information at finite chiral chemical potential $\mu_5$ constrains pseudocritical-temperature responses in the Nambu-Jona-Lasinio model under a magnetic field. Vacuum calibration alone leaves the coefficient $c_r$ of the additional interaction $\delta\Omega_r=c_r\mu_5^2(M-m_0)^2$ undetermined. We compare soft-cutoff (SC) and Pauli-Villars (PV) vacuum regularizations, each combined with the direct treatment (D) or the magnetic finite-difference scheme (MFDS). The reference SC and PV treatments exhibit opposite finite-$\mu_5$ responses already at $eB=0$. Matching the $eB=0$ scalar-susceptibility peak-temperature ratio predicted by unitarized chiral perturbation theory gives $c_{\mathrm{SC}}=-0.07112$ and $c_{\mathrm{PV}}=0.22479$. Holding these coefficients fixed at $eB=0.1,0.2,0.4$ GeV$^2$ reduces the four-treatment spread of the normalized finite-$\mu_5$-induced mass-inflection temperature change by factors of approximately $7.5$-$15.3$ at $\mu_5=0.15$ GeV and $18.1$-$32.6$ at $\mu_5=0.30$ GeV. For the distinct scalar-susceptibility peak-temperature ratio at $\mu_5=0.15$ GeV, the spread decreases by factors of approximately $74$, $27$, and $14$ at the same magnetic fields, respectively. The reduction in regularization-dependent finite-$\mu_5$ responses thus persists at the sampled nonzero magnetic fields without further matching.
authors: Jingyi Chao

papers.title: Asymmetrical transport distribution function: skewness as a key to enhance thermoelectric performance
papers.abstract: How to achieve high thermoelectric figure of merit is still a scientific challenge. By solving the Boltzmann transport equation, thermoelectric properties can be written as integrals of a single function, the transport distribution function (TDF). In this work, the shape effects of transport distribution function in various typical functional forms on thermoelectric properties of materials are systematically investigated. It is found that the asymmetry of TDF, characterized by skewness, can be used to describe universally the trend of thermoelectric properties. By defining symmetric and asymmetric TDF functions, a novel skewness is then constructed for thermoelectric applications. It is demonstrated, by comparison with ab initio calculations and experiments, that the proposed thermoelectric skewness not only perfectly captures the main feature of conventional skewness, but also is able to predict the thermoelectric power accurately. This comparison confirms the unique feature of our proposed thermoelectric skewness, as well as its special role of connection between the statistics of TDF and thermoelectric properties of materials. It is also found that the thermoelectric performance can be enhanced by increasing the asymmetry of TDF. Finally, it is also interesting to find that the thermoelectric transport properties based on typical quantum statistics (Fermi-Dirac distributions), can be well described by typical shape parameter (skewness) for classical statistics.
authors: Jin-Cheng Zheng

papers.title: Virasoro operators for relative Gromov--Witten theory
papers.abstract: Let $D$ be a smooth divisor in a smooth projective variety $X$. We construct relative Virasoro operators acting on the relative descendant potential of $(X,D)$. Each operator is the logarithmic Virasoro operator of $(X,D)$ plus a boundary correction determined only by $D$ and its normal bundle in $X$. Assuming the Virasoro conjecture for $D$, we prove that the relative constraints are equivalent to the absolute constraints for $X$. Under the same assumption, we establish compatibility with the degeneration formula for two-component projective semistable degenerations satisfying a completeness condition. Consequently, the Virasoro conjecture for the two components and the gluing divisor implies the conjecture for the general fiber. As an application, we prove the Virasoro conjecture for Enriques surfaces in every integral curve class.
authors: Shuai Guo, Longting Wu, Lei You

papers.title: Dirichlet walls beyond JT gravity and their quantum group interpretation
papers.abstract: We canonically quantize sinh dilaton gravity with finite Dirichlet boundary conditions. The reduced phase space is formulated in terms of the length of a two-sided spacelike geodesic in an effective AdS$_2$ geometry and its conjugate momentum. Canonical quantization leads to a finite-difference Schr\"odinger equation whose wavefunctions of the universe are given by $q$-hypergeometric functions. These furnish a quantum deformation of the hypergeometric wavefunctions of JT gravity. We further show that the finite cutoff Hamiltonian derived from the bulk analysis admits a natural interpretation as the reduced Casimir of $U_q(\mathfrak{sl}(2,\mathbb{R}))$ acting on hyperbolic matrix elements. The two scattering wave solutions are hyperbolic matrix elements of the modular double $U_q(\mathfrak{sl}(2,\mathbb R))\otimes U_{\tilde q}(\mathfrak{sl}(2,\mathbb R))$, and the wavefunction of the universe is their unique combination regular at vanishing length.
authors: Luca Griguolo, Jacopo Papalini, Lorenzo Russo, Domenico Seminara, Alex Tarana

papers.title: Quantum Imaging of Nonlinear Magnetization Reversal and Dissipative Domain Dynamics
papers.abstract: To investigate the rich nonlinear dynamics of magnetic materials, we introduce a stroboscopic quantum diamond microscopy technique to probe the dynamic AC response of a Pt/Co/Pt thin film using nitrogen-vacancy centres in diamond. By overcoming the limited dynamic range of conventional optically detected magnetic resonance based imaging, our approach enables the observation of magnetization reversal under various large-amplitude sinusoidal and square wave excitations. The observed phase delay between the applied field and the sample response reveals information about the energy dissipated within the material. The temporal evolution reveals magnetization reversal through domain nucleation and growth also demonstrating isolated bubble domains associated with the defects. Furthermore, the detection of higher order harmonics provides access to the nonlinear AC susceptibility. These results establish stroboscopic quantum diamond microscope as a promising tool for spatially and temporally resolving nonlinear magnetization dynamics, with potential applications extending beyond ferromagnetic systems to complex magnetic crystals, magnetic phase transitions and superconductor vortex dynamics.
authors: Manali Verma, Dasika Shishir, Prajna Shubhranshu Mahaku, P. S Anil Kumar, Kasturi Saha

papers.title: Reproducing kernel and matrix representation of the deformed quantum optical density operator of $\mathcal{R}(p,q)-$super-coherent states on $\mathcal{B}_0\oplus\mathcal{B}_1$ fermionic quantum algebra
